summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — `NewClient()` now disables TLS certificate verification for every caller, with no environment or build gate. That is a production MITM exposure on what appears to be a financial ledger client.

## Why this is blocking

`tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true}` is wired into the default `http.Transport` inside `NewClient()`. The comment says the skip is for a self-signed staging cert and points at TICKET-77, but the code path is unconditional: any binary that calls `NewClient()` (staging or production) will accept any certificate, including one presented by an on-path attacker.

Concrete failure mode: an attacker who can intercept traffic to the ledger host terminates TLS with an arbitrary cert, then reads or modifies ledger requests and responses. The client will not reject the handshake.

## What would make this acceptable

Gate the skip on an explicit non-production signal (env, config flag, or build tag), defaulting to verify-on. Prefer fixing staging properly: trust the staging CA via `RootCAs` / `x509.CertPool`, or use a real cert. A TODO comment is not a control.

## Scope note

The repo only contains `internal/ledger/client.go`; no callers or env wiring were present to soften this. Severity stands on the unconditional skip alone.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: NewClient() unconditionally sets tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: true} with only a comment about staging/TICKET-77 and no env or config gate; base used the default verifying transport, so this is a real critical TLS MITM exposure.
